rows.what_the_ink_shows: The sideways marginal paragraph was inspected as an enlarged crop rotated 90 degrees clockwise. Its formula after "les" has $H$ with a dark, looped superscript, then $(X,\Omega^p)$: the second argument has the lower horizontal arms and high central loop of a handwritten capital Omega, followed by a raised p with stem and bowl. It is not a Q with a subscript l. The exponent on H favors q (a small loop with a substantial downward stroke), but its ink is congested enough that i remains an explicitly retained alternative. The following parenthesis reads "arithmétique": the ar- opening, tall t/h strokes, and -métique ending are visible; it does not read "caractéristique". See crops/15_scan195_L304_formula.jpg and crops/15_scan195_L304_arithmetique.jpg, with context in crops/15_scan195_L304_margin.jpg.
rows.note: Correct the two transcription misreadings: replace the doubtful Q_l by Omega^p and caractéristique by arithmétique. The row proposes H^q. Both reader and main inspection find q favored but the heavily inked superscript remains unresolved against i, so the final page uses $H^{\unsure{q|i}}(X,\Omega^p)$. This explicit alternative is the final diplomatic decision, not a pending adjudication. Other existing doubts remain untouched. No Hodge-theoretic argument was used to choose the letterforms. Original-orientation crops and rotation provenance are retained.
rows.event_type: used and rechecked in this run
rows.event_outcome: Visually inspected the full scan and the rotated, enlarged, contrast-raised marginal crops. Confirmed Omega with a raised p and the parenthetical word "arithmétique"; proposed one unique-span edit for those readings and an explicit q/i doubt in the superscript of H. Classified as (a). No mathematical proof check was performed.
rows.uncertainty_note: The small superscript of H is heavily inked. Its loop and descending stroke favor q, but enlargement does not securely exclude i. After main-reader inspection, the final page retains $H^{\unsure{q|i}}$. The Omega^p and arithmétique readings are settled.
